+---
+name: implement-hybrid-model-layer
+description: Implement a new layer for the `HybridModel`. Use when the user asks you to implement a new layer. In case it's unclear which model the user refers to, ask them to clarify which model they want the layer implemented for before activating the skill.
+metadata:
+  author: Jan Ebert <janpabloe@nvidia.com>
+---
+
+<!-- Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved. -->
+
+To implement a new layer for the [`HybridModel`](../../megatron/core/models/hybrid/hybrid_model.py) in [Megatron-LM](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM), you can generally follow these steps:
+
+1. Check out [`megatron/core/models/hybrid/AGENTS.md`](../../megatron/core/models/hybrid/AGENTS.md) for general instructions on working with `HybridModel`.
+2. Check out [`docs/developer/contribute.md`](../../docs/developer/contribute.md) for general instructions on working on the codebase.
+3. Find a good place for the new layer. Generally, methods based on SSMs (state-space models) belong in [`megatron/core/ssm`](../../megatron/core/ssm). Methods based on Attention and/or Transformers belong in [`megatron/core/transformer`](../../megatron/core/transformer). `HybridModel`-specific layers belong in [`megatron/core/models/hybrid/layers`](../../megatron/core/models/hybrid/layers).
+4. Create a config class for the new layer. The new config class should subclass [`TransformerConfig`](../../megatron/core/transformer/transformer_config.py). New fields should only be added to the new config class. They should _not_ be added to `TransformerConfig` unless absolutely required.
+5. Implement the layer itself. Check out the [`parallelism-guide.md`](../../docs/user-guide/parallelism-guide.md) for settings to consider for highly parallel workloads. Consult documentation in the [`docs/user-guide/features`](../../docs/user-guide/features) directory for more in-depth feature documentation. Put kernel implementations into [`megatron/core/ops`](../../megatron/core/ops).
+6. Integrate the new layer into the [`HybridStackSubmodules`](../../megatron/core/models/hybrid/hybrid_block.py) class and the various [`ModuleSpec` setups that are provided for `HybridModel`](../../megatron/core/models/hybrid/hybrid_layer_specs.py).
+7. Integrate the new layer into the [`HybridStack.__init__`](../../megatron/core/models/hybrid/hybrid_block.py) method.
+8. Add a new symbol and mapping for the layer to the [`Symbols`](../../megatron/core/models/hybrid/layers/utils.py) class.

nodes.body: Outside this scope, but I'd still like to rework this so every new layer isn't added to every spec.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,28 @@
+---
+name: implement-hybrid-model-layer
+description: Implement a new layer for the `HybridModel`. Use when the user asks you to implement a new layer. In case it's unclear which model the user refers to, ask them to clarify which model they want the layer implemented for before activating the skill.
+metadata:
+  author: Jan Ebert <janpabloe@nvidia.com>
+---
+
+<!-- Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved. -->
+
+To implement a new layer for the [`HybridModel`](../../megatron/core/models/hybrid/hybrid_model.py) in [Megatron-LM](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM), you can generally follow these steps:
+
+1. Check out [`megatron/core/models/hybrid/AGENTS.md`](../../megatron/core/models/hybrid/AGENTS.md) for general instructions on working with `HybridModel`.
+2. Check out [`docs/developer/contribute.md`](../../docs/developer/contribute.md) for general instructions on working on the codebase.
+3. Find a good place for the new layer. Generally, methods based on SSMs (state-space models) belong in [`megatron/core/ssm`](../../megatron/core/ssm). Methods based on Attention and/or Transformers belong in [`megatron/core/transformer`](../../megatron/core/transformer). `HybridModel`-specific layers belong in [`megatron/core/models/hybrid/layers`](../../megatron/core/models/hybrid/layers).
+4. Create a config class for the new layer. The new config class should subclass [`TransformerConfig`](../../megatron/core/transformer/transformer_config.py). New fields should only be added to the new config class. They should _not_ be added to `TransformerConfig` unless absolutely required.
+5. Implement the layer itself. Check out the [`parallelism-guide.md`](../../docs/user-guide/parallelism-guide.md) for settings to consider for highly parallel workloads. Consult documentation in the [`docs/user-guide/features`](../../docs/user-guide/features) directory for more in-depth feature documentation. Put kernel implementations into [`megatron/core/ops`](../../megatron/core/ops).
+6. Integrate the new layer into the [`HybridStackSubmodules`](../../megatron/core/models/hybrid/hybrid_block.py) class and the various [`ModuleSpec` setups that are provided for `HybridModel`](../../megatron/core/models/hybrid/hybrid_layer_specs.py).
+7. Integrate the new layer into the [`HybridStack.__init__`](../../megatron/core/models/hybrid/hybrid_block.py) method.
+8. Do **not** add a new symbol and/or mapping for the layer to the [`Symbols`](../../megatron/core/models/hybrid/layers/utils.py) class. Instantiating models using patterns based on `Symbols` can be considered deprecated, so the functionality shouldn't be extended.
+9. Write tests for the new functionality. Include at least one integration test that builds and executes an actual model. Be sure to check the various permutations of parallelism settings that the layer supports.
+
+Deviate as necessary; this recipe isn't set in stone, but it should provide guidance and resources for successful integration of a new layer.
+
+Before you start the implementation, make sure you have all the necessary details. Ask the user to provide more information in case the request is not clear enough. Present questions important to resolve before starting implementation work to the user for discussion.
+
+While linking to online resources is fine, ensure that the code is understandable without external context, which includes the conversation context.
+
+When done, summarize your work to the user so they can review the new features and provide feedback. Make it easy for the user to understand trade-offs in the implementation.
